title: Valorization of kenaf (Hibiscus cannabinus L.) into high‐value therapeutic agents: an updated review on extraction techniques, phytochemicals, pharmacological activities and encapsulation technologies
content:
Abstract

Kenaf (Hibiscus cannabinus L.), an annual herbaceous plant of the Malvaceae family, is native to the tropical and subtropical regions of Asia and Africa. Traditionally, kenaf has been valued for its fibre, medicinal uses and as an ingredient in food and animal feed. Recently, there has been growing research interest in the plant's pharmacological potential, as studies have revealed a rich profile of bioactive compounds, including phenolics, flavonoids, terpenoids, tocopherols, tocotrienols, phytosterols and fatty acids. These compounds are associated with a wide range of beneficial pharmacological activities, such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, antihypertensive, antihyperlipidemic, anti-hyperpigmentation and anticancer effects. This review provides an up-to-date overview of the bioactive compounds found in kenaf, highlighting the latest advancements in extraction techniques including ultrasonication technology that can efficiently extract these beneficial phytoconstituents. Furthermore, the paper explores the pharmacological activities associated with kenaf, investigating the therapeutic potential of its secondary metabolites. The review also discusses recent developments in encapsulation technologies particularly on the application of spray drying, extrusion and nanotechnology, which can enhance the bioavailability and therapeutic efficacy of kenaf's bioactive compounds, making them suitable for applications in the pharmaceutical and nutraceutical industries. © 2025 Society of Chemical Industry.
